questions.q: By the end of this capstone, what is FeedbackScope, per this lesson?
options: An untested prototype that never actually ran
A manually-scaled service with no autoscaling policy
A containerized, deployed, and autoscaled service where every configuration choice has a stated reason
A service that still runs on the developer's laptop only
questions.explain: That's the lesson's own summary of what the two prior lessons actually produced -- not just a running service, but one with justified configuration.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the 'strong' interview answer about FeedbackScope is better than the 'weak' one?
options: It's shorter and easier to memorize
It shows specific decisions and their reasons, not just a list of steps taken
It avoids mentioning any technical details at all
It focuses only on the model's accuracy score
questions.explain: The strong answer explains why concurrency was chosen over CPU and why caching was skipped -- decisions an interviewer can actually probe, unlike a generic 'I built and deployed it.'

questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes a README more than just 'how to run this'?
options: Including the full source code pasted directly into the README
Listing every dependency version number in exhaustive detail
Omitting any mention of the autoscaling policy entirely
Explaining the Dockerfile and autoscaling policy choices, with their reasons
questions.explain: The lesson's point: the reasoning behind the choices is the actual portfolio piece, not just instructions for running the code.

questions.q: What part of the AI Engineer path does this lesson say this course closes out?
options: The entire AI Engineer path, with nothing left after this course
The infrastructure side -- the app can now run somewhere, survive a release, and scale
Only the Docker fundamentals from Chapter 1, nothing from later chapters
The data science and modeling side of the path
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this course as closing the infrastructure piece -- deployment, release safety, and scaling -- not the whole path.
